questions.q: Why doesn't Snowflake's built-in classification recognize a format like Placekey on its own?
options: Placekey is an organization/industry-specific identifier format that no generic, built-in classifier was taught to recognize
Placekey columns are always encrypted and unreadable
Built-in classification only works on numeric columns
Placekey is a Snowflake system tag, so it is always auto-applied
questions.explain: Built-in classification recognizes common, generic sensitive patterns. Organization- or partner-specific formats like Placekey require a custom classifier taught to recognize that specific pattern.

questions.q: What object type is created to hold a custom classifier's logic?
options: SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER
A masking policy
A row access policy
A stored procedure in the information_schema
questions.explain: A custom classifier is created as a SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER instance in your own schema, then taught a pattern with ADD_REGEX.

questions.q: What five pieces of information does ADD_REGEX require to teach a custom classifier a new pattern?
options: A semantic category name, a privacy category, the regex pattern, a column-name-pattern hint, and a description
A table name, a column name, a role name, a warehouse name, and a schema name
Only the regex pattern — everything else is optional
A masking policy name and the columns it should apply to
questions.explain: ADD_REGEX takes the invented semantic category ('PLACEKEY'), the privacy category ('IDENTIFIER'), the regex itself, an optional column-name regex hint, and a human-readable description.

questions.q: How is a custom classifier actually run against a table, once it has been registered?
options: By listing it in the custom_classifiers option of an ordinary SYSTEM$CLASSIFY call, alongside Snowflake's built-in classifiers
It runs automatically on a schedule with no SYSTEM$CLASSIFY call needed
By calling ADD_REGEX a second time against the target table
Custom classifiers cannot be combined with SYSTEM$CLASSIFY and must be run separately
questions.explain: CALL SYSTEM$CLASSIFY('raw_pos.location', {'custom_classifiers': ['placekey'], 'auto_tag':true}) runs the custom classifier in the same call as the built-in ones.

questions.q: Once a custom classifier's tag has been applied to a column, how do you query for it?
options: The same TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS pattern used for manually applied tags and built-in classification tags
A separate, custom-classifier-only query function that doesn't work on other tag types
Custom classifier tags cannot be queried, only viewed in the SYSTEM$CLASSIFY JSON output
By calling ADD_REGEX again to list applied tags
questions.explain: Regardless of a tag's origin — manual, built-in classification, or a custom classifier — TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS is the consistent query pattern used to look it up.
